To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a heuristic approach to intrusion detection can be effective for detecting attacks in encrypted networks, and that the effectiveness of this approach can be significantly improved by the use of a network wide view of the network traffic.

(1) a network can be monitored for intrusion detection purposes even when all traffic is encrypted end-to-end, (2) the network traffic can be monitored without the use of a trusted network device or a man-in-the-middle, and (3) the network traffic does not have to be decrypted in order to be monitored.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to secure a network when it is not possible to see what is going on.
the development and testing of a network intrusion detection system for a fully encrypted network environment.
the following question: How can network intrusion detection be performed on a network carrying only encrypted traffic?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have shown that a heuristic approach to network intrusion detection, based on the concept of network-wide normal behavior, is a valid and effective approach for detecting intrusions on a network where the vast majority of the traffic is host-to-host encrypted.
in a world of ubiquitous end-to-end encryption the current network intrusion detection model will not be sufficient.
the network security model needs to change to one that describes what the network looks and feels like under normal conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model is capable of detecting a wide range of intrusions and anomalies in encrypted traffic.
the proposed model for detecting network anomalies in a completely encrypted network environment is feasible.
the network intrusion detection model needs to change from signature-based detection to a model that flags deviations for further investigation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the network intrusion detection systems of tomorrow will need to be able to monitor encrypted traffic.
the current network intrusion detection model is inadequate for the coming IPv6 world.
the network security community needs to start thinking about the problem of network anomaly detection rather than intrusion detection.
